description: Composite figure of two panels documenting texture evolution in cold-rolled Fe–30Mn–11Al–1.2C. (a) is a 3 x 5 grid of orientation distribution function (ODF) constant-φ2 sections: rows are φ2 = 0°, 45°, 65° and columns the cold rolling reductions 10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 90%; arrows at top-left mark the φ1 (horizontal) and φ (vertical) directions of Euler space. A colour bar at the right ranks contour levels 1 (grey) to 9 (dark red). Red annotations mark the α-fiber dashed line across the whole φ2 = 0° row, "B" and "G" in the 30% φ2 = 0° section, "Cu" and "CuT" in the φ2 = 45° row, "S" in the 50% φ2 = 65° section, and a γ-fiber dashed line with "E" in the 90% φ2 = 45° section. Contour density and colour grade rise strongly with reduction, the 90% sections containing level 8-9 cores. (b) plots f(g) versus φ1 [°] (0-90, ticks every 15°) with f(g) from 0 to 10; five symbol-coded curves, the diamond curve peaking between the 8 and 10 gridlines at low φ1 while the square curve stays at about 1-2. Corner text reads α-fiber, <110>//ND, Φ=45°, φ2=0°; a thick red arrow points up-left. Together the panels demonstrate α-fiber strengthening and a copper-type to brass-type texture transition.

subfigures.description: Grid of 15 ODF sections arranged as 3 rows (φ2 = 0°, 45°, 65°) by 5 columns (cold rolling reduction 10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 90%), drawn as contour maps with a 9-level colour scale (grey = 1 to dark red = 9). Red annotations: α-fiber dashed line across the φ2 = 0° row, B and G in the 30% φ2 = 0° section, Cu and CuT in the φ2 = 45° row, S in the 50% φ2 = 65° section, γ-fiber dashed line with E in the 90% φ2 = 45° section. Texture intensity clearly grows with rolling reduction.

Line plot of texture intensity f(g) (y-axis 0-10, gridlines every 2) versus φ1 [°] (x-axis 0-90, labelled every 15°) with five symbol-coded curves; the diamond-marked curve reaches the highest f(g) (between the 8 and 10 gridlines) around low-to-medium φ1, magenta and green triangle curves are intermediate, blue diamonds span mid-range and black squares stay lowest at about 1-2. A corner text box reads α-fiber, <110>//ND, Φ=45°, φ2=0°; a thick red arrow points up and left toward the highest curve. The legend does not state which curve belongs to which rolling reduction.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a 3-row x 5-column matrix of ODF sections, rows labelled φ2 = 0°, φ2 = 45°, φ2 = 65° and columns headed 10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 90%.
Panel (a) carries a discrete grey-to-red colour scale with nine levels labelled 1 to 9, where 1 is grey and 9 is dark red, i.e. ODF intensity increases from 1 to 9.
Within every φ2 row of (a) the contour density and colour level increase with rolling reduction, the strongest (level 8-9, orange-red) cores appearing in the 70% and 90% columns.
A red dashed line labelled 'α-fiber' runs horizontally across all five sections of the φ2 = 0° row of (a).

Red text annotations 'B' and 'G' are placed on the 30% section of the φ2 = 0° row of (a); 'S' is annotated on the 50% section of the φ2 = 65° row; 'Cu' and 'CuT' are annotated in the φ2 = 45° row (Cu on the 50% section, CuT below it); a dashed line labelled 'γ-fiber' with label 'E' marks the 90% section of the φ2 = 45° row.

Panel (b) has axes f(g) (0 to 10, labelled every 2) versus φ1 [°] (0 to 90, labelled every 15°) and contains five curves distinguished by symbol (dark-red diamonds, magenta triangles, green triangles, blue diamonds, black squares).

In panel (b) the diamond-marked curve attains the largest f(g), rising to a maximum just below the 10 gridline in the low-φ1 region, while the black-square curve remains the lowest over the whole φ1 range at roughly the 1 to 2 gridlines.
The text box inside panel (b) prints 'α-fiber', '<110>//ND', 'Φ=45°' and 'φ2=0°', and a thick red arrow points up and to the left toward the highest curve.
The caption states that the figure shows selected ODF sections of φ2 = 0°, 45°, 65° for various cold rolling reduction, and names only part (a).
The capturing text states the α-fiber texture increased monotonously up to 90% rolling reduction (Fig. 8).
The capturing text states the {112}<111> copper (Cu) and {123}<111> S components (belonging to the β-fiber) increased at lower to medium rolling reductions and then decreased at higher strains.

The capturing text states that there is a transition from copper-type to brass-type texture at 50% cold rolling reduction, characterised by a gradual decrease of Cu and S, and that weak orientations near the γ-fiber appear at 90% rolling reduction.

The capturing text states the initial texture before cold rolling was almost random, as reflected by the inverse pole figure in Fig. 2(a), and that the whole texture intensity is weaker than in copper alloys and nickel.
